sections.Kurzabstract: The PTED scale, as a self-report questionnaire, contains 19 items for assessing the functions of embitterment reactions to negative life events. The questionnaire contains 19 individual statements. Reliability: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = .93) and test-retest reliability (Spearman rho correlation was .71 for the total score, with a range of .53-.86 for individual items) were high. Validity: The PTED scale discriminated significantly between patients who, according to clinical assessment, suffered from pathological embitterment. Correlations with related instruments showed good convergent validity. The data of the non-clinical sample showed a prevalence of clinically relevant embitterment in the general population of 2.5%. The PTED scale allows a valid measurement of embitterment as an emotional reaction to a negative life event. In addition, the results show that reactive embitterment in connection with a negative life event is a widespread phenomenon in clinical and non-clinical populations.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The Post-Traumatic Embitterment Disorder Selbstbeurteilungsfragebogen (PTED Skala) asks about persistent and impairing embitterment reactions in the aftermath of negative life events.
sections.Aufbau: The PTED self-report questionnaire contains 19 items for assessing the functions of embitterment reactions to negative life events. The questionnaire is completed by the patients themselves and begins with the line "In den vergangenen Jahren hatte ich ein einschneidendes Lebensereignis zu verkraften, ..." followed by 19 individual statements (to be answered on a 5-point scale: 0 does not apply, 1 hardly applies, 2 partly applies, 3 applies, 4 fully applies). A mean score of > = 2.5 indicates a clinically significant intensity of reactive embitterment.
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The PTED scale was administered to four independent samples of patients and control persons. Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were high. A factor analysis suggested a two-factor solution that explained 55.25% of the total variance.
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien: The PTED scale discriminated significantly between patients who, according to clinical assessment, suffered from pathological embitterment. Correlations with related instruments showed good convergent validity. The data from the non-clinical sample showed a prevalence of clinically relevant embitterment in the general population of 2.5%. The PTED scale allows a reliable and valid measurement of embitterment as an emotional reaction to a negative life event. In addition, the results show that reactive embitterment in connection with a negative life event is a widespread phenomenon in clinical and non-clinical populations.
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund:
Negative life events can evoke very different psychological reactions, ranging from good coping to anxiety, depression or post-traumatic stress disorders (PTSD) (Bale, 2006; Boelen & Lensvelt-Mulders, 2005; Mancini & Bonanno, 2006; Mol et al., 2005; Viinameaki, Koskela, Niskanen, & Taehkae, 1994). One response to this can be embitterment, a feeling that most people know. Like anxiety, depression or stress reactions, the feeling of embitterment can become pathological when its intensity increases and feelings of helplessness, dysphoric mood, intrusive thoughts, aggression, suicidal thoughts, withdrawal from others, phobic avoidance of places or persons that remind one of the negative event occur, or when it is accompanied by somatic complaints (Hauer, Wessel, & Merckelbach, 2006).
Linden, Baumann, Lieberei and Rotter (2009) described and summarised this clinical syndrome as "post-traumatic embitterment disorder" (engl. Post-traumatic embitterment disorder, PTED) (Linden, 2003; Linden, Baumann, Lieberei & Rotter, 2009; Linden, Baumann, Rotter & Schippan, 2007a, 2007b). PTED is regarded as a subtype of adjustment disorder and as a reaction to a severe, yet normal negative experience, such as unemployment, divorce or the death of a loved one.
The frequent commonality of such events is that they are experienced as unjustified and unfair and that they violate basic beliefs (Beck, Rush, Shaw & Emery, 1979; Janoff-Bulman, 1992) or overvalued schemata (Dalgleish, 2004; Dalgleish & Power, 2004).
The pathogenic mechanism of PTED does not lie in the characteristics of the event, but occurs when there is a match between the patient's ideas and value system on the one hand and the violation of these ideas by the negative event on the other. PTED, like PTSD, is characterised not by a specific stressful life event, but by various psychological processes (experiences of injustice and humiliation) and by a severe specific psychopathological profile (embitterment). Linden et al. (2009) were the first to describe an instrument that asks about embitterment and associated psychological symptoms in response to a stressful life event, namely the PTED self-report questionnaire.
sections.Testkonzept/Testaufbau:
The PTED self-report questionnaire is available in paper-pencil format and contains 19 items for assessing the functions of embitterment reactions to negative life events.
The questionnaire is completed by the patients themselves and begins with the line "In den vergangenen Jahren hatte ich ein einschneidendes Lebensereignis zu verkraften, ..." followed by 19 individual statements. The participant is asked to rate these on a 5-point scale (0 does not apply, 1 hardly applies, 2 partly applies, 3 applies, 4 fully applies) and not to omit any item. A total mean score of > = 2.5 on the PTED scale indicates a clinically significant intensity of reactive embitterment.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus: For scoring, the point scores assigned to the responses are added up and divided by the number of items.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: Special scoring aids are not necessary.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Scoring takes only a few minutes per questionnaire.
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: The instrument can be administered as an individual or group test. In addition to the German version of the PTED self-report scale, there are translations into Turkish, Korean, Croatian and English. The German version also has a diagnostic interview.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The instrument is designed for adults from 18 years of age.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: Administration, including the time for instructions, takes only a few minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion: The questionnaire is preceded by a very short instruction: "In den vergangenen Jahren hatte ich ein einschneidendes Lebensereignis zu verkraften, ..."
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge: No specific requirements are placed on the test administrator.
sections.Testkonstruktion: To examine the frequency and intensity of embitterment, the PTED scale was given to four independent samples: an inpatient PTED group (n = 49) with a matched control group (n = 48), selected by a clinical interview at the Heinrich-Heine-Klinik Potsdam; a group of unselected inpatients "UI" (n = 100) who suffered from other mental illnesses; a group of patients treated in a normal practice "GP" (n = 221); and a train sample "TS" (n = 158). The TS sample comprises a group of randomly selected persons travelling on a public train and is used as an estimate of embitterment in the general population. Here, 34.8% remembered a recent experience that evoked feelings of embitterment; 2.5% had a score of 2 or higher on the PTED scale, which indicates a PTED condition.
sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: Owing to the questionnaire format, the standardised procedure and the written instructions, the instrument can claim objectivity with regard to its administration and scoring.
sections.Gütekriterien/Reliabilität: The reliability of the PTED scale was determined by measuring internal consistency. In addition, a test-retest calculation was carried out with the UI sample. The alpha coefficient was .93 and indicates high internal consistency. The Spearman rho correlation was .71 for the total score, with a range of .53-.86 for individual items. This speaks for a good test-retest reliability of the PTED scale.
sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
The validity of the test was tested by a discriminant analysis of the PTED sample and the control group. A chi-square transformation of Wilks' lambda showed that the two groups differed significantly (chi-square = 76.94, p < 0.001). Of the 49 patients from the PTED group, 44 were diagnosed with PTED on the basis of the scale, as were 4 of the 48 patients from the control group. This indicates a sensitivity of the scale of 89.8% and a specificity of 91.7%. In general, the predicted classification of the PTED scale was in agreement with the clinical diagnosis.
The discriminant function indicated a total mean score of 1.6 as the critical value between the two groups. With regard to clinical applicability and in order to increase specificity, a mean score of 2.5 on the scale is recommended as the cut-off value. A value of > = 2.5 indicates a clinically significant intensity of reactive embitterment.
Moderate to high correlations were found consistently for every item. Particularly high correlations were found for items that ask about intrusive memories (items 5, 19 and 4), feelings of disempowerment, helplessness and injustice (items 12, 8, 3) and deterioration of mood and numbness (items 9, 15, 16). These results reflect the three characteristic features of PTED symptomatology:
the central role of negative life events, which frequently evoke painful and intrusive memories;
the feeling of helplessness and injustice caused by the event;
the resulting deterioration of psychological well-being.
The convergent validity of the PTED scale was tested in the PTED and control groups by comparison with the Bern Embitterment Scale (BVI; Znoj, 2009), a modified version of the Impact of Event Scale (IES-R; Maercker & Schützwohl, 1998) and the Symptom Checkliste SCL-90-R (Derogatis, 1977; German version Franke, 1995). The PTED scale correlated significantly (p < 0.001) with the IES scale (r = .76) and the Bern Embitterment Scale (r = .67). In addition, significant correlations were found between the PTED scale and global indices of the SCL-90-R. The PTED scale correlated with the GSI (Global Severity Index, measures general psychological burden) (r = .57), the PST (Positive Symptom Total, records the number of symptoms for which a burden is present) (r = .53) and with the SCL depression scale (r = .52). This speaks for good convergent validity.
An exploratory principal component analysis with all items of the PTED scale was carried out on the UI sample in order to determine the factorial structure. The number of factors to be extracted was determined by the "scree plot method" (Cattell, 1966). Two factors emerged, which explained 55.25% of the total variance. Factor 1 was defined by items that ask about psychological status and social functioning. Factor 2 contains items that ask about emotional reaction to an event and thoughts of revenge. This factor solution contains the two core dimensions of reactive embitterment: the pathological emotional reaction following a negative event and the resulting impairment of well-being and social functions (Linden, Rotter, Baumann & Lieberei, 2007). It therefore seems appropriate that the severity of reactive embitterment and the symptomatology of PTED be evaluated by a total score of the scale.
sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten: The Post-Traumatic Embitterment Disorder Selbstbeurteilungsfragebogen (PTED Skala) asks about persistent and impairing embitterment reactions in the aftermath of negative life events.
sections.Bewertung:
Embitterment is an emotion that is probably familiar to everyone. The data of Linden et al. (2009) suggest that a third of the general population remember feelings of embitterment and that in a quarter this occurs in a more intense form (PTED total score > 1). However, only 2-3% were found with a form of reactive embitterment of clinically relevant intensity. Accordingly, embitterment should be understood as a dimensional phenomenon, similar to anxiety or depressed mood.
The PTED scale is an instrument that can be used for a classification of reactive embitterment and its severity. Based on the results of the UI and GP samples, it can be assumed that some cases diagnosed as depression or phobia are actually cases of PTED (Power & Tarsia, 2007). In such cases, the PTED scale can draw physicians' attention to these special aspects of the illness and entail corresponding consequences for treatment (Linden, Baumann, & Schippan, 2006; Linden, Rotter et al., 2007; Schippan, Baumann, & Linden, 2004). The data suggest that a mean total score of > = 2.5 on the PTED scale indicates a clinically significant intensity of reactive embitterment.
Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were high. The construct validity of the scale was shown by the level of agreement (90.7%) with clinical assessments. Convergent validity was shown by significant correlations with the Bern Embitterment Scale, the IES and the SCL-90-R.
In interpreting the study, it should be taken into account that the data were collected with two different versions of the PTED scale (17- and 19-item versions). The instructions in each sample were standardised and every participant signed a declaration of consent. However, a 17-item version was given to the PTED and GP groups, of which two items were later each split into two items for reasons of clarity. This resulted in a version of 19 items, which was given to the UI and GP samples. This could be a limitation of the study, although it is unlikely that the results were influenced by it.

Study.Instructions:
Bitte beantworten Sie die folgenden Aussagen und Feststellungen und kreuzen Sie die für Sie zutreffende Spalte an. Bitte lassen Sie keine Zeile aus!
In den vergangenen Jahren hatte ich ein einschneidendes Lebensereignis zu verkraften,

PTEDSKALA01.Description: das mich äußerst gekränkt oder verbittert hat.

PTEDSKALA02.Description: wodurch sich meine psychische Befindlichkeit deutlich und bis heute negativ verändert hat.

PTEDSKALA03.Description: das aus meiner Sicht äußerst ungerecht oder nicht fair war.

PTEDSKALA04.Description: an das ich immer wieder denken muss.

PTEDSKALA05.Description: das mich heftig aufregt, wenn ich daran erinnert werde.

PTEDSKALA06.Description: das in mir Gedanken an Rache auslöst.

PTEDSKALA07.Description: wegen dem ich mir Vorwürfe mache und ärgerlich auf mich selbst bin.

PTEDSKALA08.Description: weswegen ich häufiger das Gefühl habe, dass es keinen Sinn macht, Dinge anzupacken und sich anzustrengen.

PTEDSKALA09.Description: durch das meine Stimmung häufig niedergeschlagen und gedrückt ist.

PTEDSKALA10.Description: das dazu geführt hat, dass ich mich in allgemein schlechter körperlicher Verfassung fühle.

PTEDSKALA11.Description: weswegen ich bestimmte Orte oder Personen meide, um nicht daran erinnert zu werden.

PTEDSKALA12.Description: dem gegenüber ich mich ohnmächtig und hilflos ausgeliefert fühle.

PTEDSKALA13.Description: das in mir Gefühle der Genugtuung auslöst, beim Gedanken, der Verursacher würde einmal Ähnliches erleiden.

PTEDSKALA14.Description: das dazu geführt hat, dass meine Kraft und mein Antrieb reduziert und nicht mehr wie früher sind.

PTEDSKALA15.Description: das dazu geführt hat, dass ich gereizter bin als früher.

PTEDSKALA16.Description: weshalb ich mich ablenken muss, wenn ich vorübergehend eine normale und ausgeglichene Stimmung erleben will.

PTEDSKALA17.Description: das dazu geführt hat, dass ich meinen beruflichen und/oder familiären Aktivitäten nicht mehr wie früher nachgehe.

PTEDSKALA18.Description: das dazu geführt hat, dass ich mich von Freunden und geselligen Aktivitäten zurückgezogen habe.

PTEDSKALA19.Description: . zu dem sich mir immer wieder belastende Erinnerungen aufdrängen
